sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Elf is a word for the people of the Otherworld. The name reached Britain from Scandinavia with the Viking raiders and immigrants. The term became naturalized in Britain. People used it as often as fairy and brownie. The small, transparent ellyll usually worked alone, yet the ellyllon could gather under their queen Mab to dance as troopers.
